\[
f(n)=aB+c.
\]
We need
\[
aB+c=10a+c \implies a(B-10)=0.
\]
Since \(a>0\), we need \(B=10\), so the greatest digit must be \(9\). Thus every two-digit number containing a digit \(9\) works. There are \(18\) such numbers.

For a three-digit number \(n=100a+10t+c\), let \(B\) be the base. Then
\[
f(n)=aB^2+tB+c.
\]
We need
\[
aB^2+tB+c=100a+10t+c
\]

\[
a(B^2-100)+t(B-10)=0
\]
\[
(B-10)\bigl(a(B+10)+t\bigr)=0.
\]
Since \(a(B+10)+t>0\), we must have \(B=10\), meaning the greatest digit is \(9\). Therefore every three-digit number containing a digit \(9\) works.
